outcome: No proof or disproof of the infinitude of Wagstaff primes has appeared since 26 January 2024; only record-extension and unrelated computational/related-problem work occurred.
summary: The question is a pure existence/infinitude claim, and per §3.1 it is only moved by an actual proof of infinitude, not by new examples, larger records, or verification to a higher computational horizon. I confirmed no such proof exists: the Wikipedia article's conjecture statement is unchanged and undated, and no paper claiming to settle the infinitude of Wagstaff primes was found on arXiv, in expert blogs, or in prime-number databases. What did happen since the frozen revision is entirely record-keeping and adjacent computation, none of which changes the bullet: (1) a new largest known Wagstaff (probable) prime, (2^141079+1)/3 with 42,469 digits, was found by ECPP in October 2025 (t5k.org/top20/page.php?id=67), surpassing the January-2024-era record of (2^138937+1)/3 (October 2023, already in Wikipedia's frozen text) — a record extension of an infinitude question, explicitly excluded by §3.1; (2) Alexey Dolotov, 'Three Brillhart-Lehmer-Selfridge primality proofs for Wagstaff numbers' (arXiv 2605.18555, submitted 18 May 2026), gives classical N-1 primality certificates for three specific Wagstaff numbers (W_2617, W_10501, W_12391) as an alternative to ECPP, and states all Wagstaff numbers with exponents up to 42737 have now been proved prime or composite — pure classical/computational number theory with no AI, ML, or LLM component mentioned anywhere in the abstract or body; (3) Herbert Batte, 'On Wagstaff primes in the k-Lucas number sequence' (arXiv 2602.20387, submitted 23 February 2026), proves Wagstaff primes appear in generalized k-Lucas sequences only in finitely many specific cases, using linear forms in logarithms and LLL reduction — this is a related/variant problem (intersection with a different sequence family), not a case of or bound on the stated infinitude question, so it is correctly out of scope per §3.1's case-vs-variant rule. The 2019 vixra manuscript by Stephen Marshall claiming a proof of infinitude, flagged by triage, both predates the window (2019, well before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision) and remains unreviewed/unpublished, so even had it fallen inside the window it would not meet the resolved/claimed bar under §6.1. No AI system was found near this problem in any capacity — not in the record search, not in the primality proofs, not in the k-Lucas paper.
competing_reading: One could argue the Dolotov BLS paper's methodological contribution (giving primality proofs independent of ECPP) is itself 'progress' on the broader project of proving Wagstaff primality without conjectural tools, but it does not move the infinitude question itself, which is what this bullet asks, so I classified it as not a change to this problem rather than as `progress`.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint that proves (or disproves) that there are infinitely many primes p for which (2^p+1)/3 is prime — nothing short of that changes this bullet's status.
